headline: 4 detained after AL activists detonate crude bombs in Mohakhali
summary: Police arrested four people, including a woman, after a flash procession by banned Awami League activists in Dhaka.

caption:
Four people detained in Dhaka after banned AL activists detonated crude bombs during a flash procession.

Police detained four people, including a woman, after activists of the banned Awami League and its affiliated organisations staged a flash procession in Dhaka’s Mohakhali area this morning.

According to Mahbubur Rahman, officer-in-charge of Tejgaon Industrial Area Police Station, three to four crude bombs were detonated during the procession.

Witnesses report the march began around 9:00 am in front of the icddr,b building and moved through the nearby bus terminal.

The activists carried banners with the Awami League name and chanted 'Joy Bangla' slogans, demanding the lifting of the ban on the party's activities.

Members of the Mohila League also reportedly joined the march near the terminal before the crude bombs were detonated and the group left the area.

headline: SSC and HSC exams to have uniform question papers across Bangladesh
summary: Education Minister A N M Ehsanul Haq Milan announced the move to ensure fairness and consistency across all education boards.
details: Education Minister A N M Ehsanul Haq Milan announced on Thursday that all general education boards in Bangladesh will now use the same question papers for SSC and HSC examinations.
Speaking at a press conference at the Secretariat, the minister explained that the move aims to eliminate disparities where some boards might set easier or harder questions than others.
He compared the system to international standards, citing the 'O' and 'A' level exams conducted globally with uniform question papers.
The minister also confirmed that the recent secondary (SSC) exams were conducted successfully without any question paper leaks.
The results for the secondary examinations are scheduled to be published on July 20.
To reduce session jams, the government is arranging for SSC and HSC exams to take place immediately after the completion of the syllabus.
As part of this effort, the schedules for 2027 have already been announced: SSC exams will begin on January 7, 2027, and HSC exams will start on June 6, 2027.
caption:
No more board-specific difficulty levels. SSC and HSC exams will now feature the same questions for everyone nationwide.

Education Minister A N M Ehsanul Haq Milan announced on Thursday that all general education boards in Bangladesh will now use the same question papers for SSC and HSC examinations.

Speaking at a press conference at the Secretariat, the minister explained that the move aims to eliminate disparities where some boards might set easier or harder questions than others.

He compared the system to international standards, citing the 'O' and 'A' level exams conducted globally with uniform question papers.

The minister also confirmed that the recent secondary (SSC) exams were conducted successfully without any question paper leaks.

The results for the secondary examinations are scheduled to be published on July 20.

To reduce session jams, the government is arranging for SSC and HSC exams to take place immediately after the completion of the syllabus.

As part of this effort, the schedules for 2027 have already been announced: SSC exams will begin on January 7, 2027, and HSC exams will start on June 6, 2027.

Source: Prothom Alo, Somoy News, Jamuna TV
